# vk v0.2.2

Date: 2026-10-20. Status: Experimental Git release.
Workspace packages `vkrust` and `vkrust-gen` use version 0.2.2; the Rust import
namespace is `vk`. This Git release does not publish to crates.io.

## Native API

All 137 Vulkan 1.0 command spellings in the pinned Khronos registry now have
public native operations. This release adds 58 paired wrappers for graphics,
render passes/framebuffers, drawing, queries, sparse operations, byte payloads
and enumerations, alongside the prior development batch's 30 timeline,
synchronization2 and copy2 operations. Free functions and methods share one
cached-PFN implementation. Partial pipeline outputs, native non-error statuses,
fixed array extents and checked slice/count relationships are preserved.

The total wrapper surface is 182 of 842 exact registry command spellings.
Remaining commands are accessible through raw PFNs. Vulkan 1.2, including the
remaining 1.1 operations, is the next command-coverage target; complete later-core
and extension wrappers remain open.

## Loading and ownership

Owned creation snapshots record API ceilings, extension enablement and exact
typed feature records. Dispatch admission preserves independent alias spellings
and filters cached tables once. Feature requirements can be checked explicitly;
promotion equivalence and cross-feature dependencies are not inferred.

External handles can be imported with truthful owned metadata. Import errors
preserve caller ownership. Native creation preflights metadata/resolvers and
either rolls back initialization failures or returns the surviving handle and
library ownership for explicit recovery. Enumerations retry within a bounded
budget and report instability rather than silently returning partial results.

Native destruction remains explicit; Drop never submits, waits or destroys
Vulkan resources. All operations retain their documented unsafe Vulkan
obligations. Public error enums gain variants in this experimental release;
downstream exhaustive matches may require updating.

## Verification and limits

The runtime checkpoint passes 270 workspace tests, independent pinned-header
ABI checks (1,447 records, 9,267 layout/value comparisons, 348 bitfield byte
comparisons), generator freshness/order checks, and native compute/readback and
timeline/import workloads. Native cache serialization/import/merge, event and
fence status, and render-pass/framebuffer object checks also pass. Separate core
and synchronization validation profiles report no validation warnings/errors.
The resulting release commit is built/tested and its actual Cargo package is
checked through an external consumer before tagging.

Native evidence applies to x86-64 Linux, Intel HD Graphics 4400/Haswell,
Vulkan 1.2.354 and Mesa 26.2.3. Mesa reports incomplete Haswell support. Graphics
pipeline execution/drawing, synchronization2/copy2 GPU workloads, presentation,
positive video execution, protected-platform ABIs and broader drivers/targets
are not qualified by these checks. No Vulkan conformance, full production
qualification, performance superiority or VMA equivalence is claimed.

The canonical design retains future research into Rust construction/lifetime
safety and NVIDIA CUDA Rust resource/completion patterns, without adding an
execution framework or changing the native Vulkan foundation in this release.
